rule: Product code stays closed until the plan is approved. Missing information is a spec defect: ask, don't peek at the implementation.
good: read specs/<ID>.md, write the plan, wait for approval; ask when the spec is silent

rule: After the plan — stop and wait for approval. Code only after an explicit “ok”.
good: plan as a table → stop → after “ok” write the code

rule: Never say “tests pass” without running the test runner immediately before. Paste the full output.
good: run the suite and paste the output, then say what it means

rule: After a test fails, do not edit it. First three hypotheses: product bug / test bug / spec defect — then wait for a decision.
good: state three hypotheses — product bug / test bug / spec defect — and wait

rule: Don't present tests as done until they have been run. No environment to run them — say so and mark the code as a draft.
good: run the tests, or say plainly that they are a draft nobody has executed

rule: Change only files from the approved plan. Need another file — say so first.
good: touch only the files listed in the approved plan

rule: More than three edits to one file — stop and explain what is unclear instead of trying again.
good: after the third edit of one file, stop and say what is unclear

rule: Don't write “I assume” / “let's say”. If the spec doesn't define behaviour, ask and stop.
good: ask: “the spec does not define X — which behaviour is correct?”

rule: If the user corrected you — restate the task in your own words and wait for confirmation before continuing.
good: restate the task in your own words and wait for confirmation

rule: In a testing task, do not change the product code. A failing test is a finding: report it as a possible product bug and wait — a quiet fix hides it.
good: report it and wait: “R3 fails — the total ignores the discount. Product bug?”

rule: Don't update snapshots to make a failing test pass. A snapshot diff is a finding: show it, say whether the change is intended, and update only after the user agrees.
good: show the snapshot diff and ask: “the total moved under the table — intended?”; update only after a yes

rule: Don't loosen the test runner's config to get green: no more retries, no longer timeouts, no excluded tests. A flaky or slow test is a finding to report.
good: keep retries: 0 and the timeouts; report “checkout.spec.ts times out at 30 s — slow backend or a real hang?”

rule: Do not weaken existing assertions (== → in, concrete value → ANY / is not None, removing checks). A failing assertion calls for triage, not an edit.
good: keep the assertion and triage the failure instead

rule: Assert only concrete values from the specification. “Didn't crash”, “not empty”, “status < 500” are forbidden.
good: expect(r.status()).toBe(423) and expect(body.reason).toBe('too_many_attempts')

rule: No sleep with a constant and no skip / retry. Wait only via wait_until() from helpers.
good: await expect(locator).toBeVisible() — wait for a condition, not for a number

rule: Don't assert concrete dates or changing content. Assert a pattern or move the value to config.
good: expect(text).toMatch(/Deadline .+ \d{4}/) or read the date from config

rule: Don't make a test depend on timing or page internals: no waitUntil: 'networkidle', exact element counts, force: true, element handles, eval or waits without a timeout. Wait for and act on a specific element, as a user would.
good: await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Pay' }).click(); await expect(page.getByRole('heading', { name: 'Paid' })).toBeVisible()

rule: An expected failure hides a live bug behind a green suite. Report the bug first and say in the test which ticket keeps it red.
good: file the bug, then keep the test red with a comment naming the ticket

rule: Numbers in assertions come only from the spec, with a comment or a named constant.
good: const MAX_ATTEMPTS = 5; expect(attempts).toBe(MAX_ATTEMPTS)

rule: More than two assertions in a test — give each a message saying what it checks.
good: expect(status, 'lockout status').toBe(423)

rule: No if/for inside a test. One test — one path; variants via parametrisation.
good: one test per path; use test.each / a loop over cases outside the test body

rule: Don't repeat the same assertion. Different input — different test.
good: assert once per fact; a second input deserves a second test

rule: Locate by role, label or exact text. A CSS selector is a guess about markup and breaks on the next redesign.
good: page.getByRole('link', { name: 'About us', exact: true })

rule: Do not select by position (.first(), .nth()). Narrow the locator until it matches one element.
good: page.getByRole('navigation').getByRole('link', { name: 'About us' })

rule: Every test must check what happened. A test that clicks, taps, types or sends a request with no assertion anywhere in it verifies nothing — it only proves nothing crashed.
good: await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Pay' }).click(); await expect(page.getByText('Paid')).toBeVisible();

rule: Reset app state between tests: beforeEach(() => device.reloadReactNative()) or device.launchApp({ newInstance: true }). Without it, one test's leftover state can make the next one flaky or order-dependent.
good: beforeEach(async () => { await device.reloadReactNative(); });

rule: A method that reads like a test (its name starts with "test", in a class named ...Test/Tests/IT) needs an actual @Test (or other JUnit/TestNG lifecycle) annotation. Without one, the runner silently never calls it — the suite stays green while this method never ran at all.
good:
@Test
public void shouldLogIn() { ... }

rule: Never leave a catch block empty (or with only a comment). If an exception is truly expected and safe to ignore, say so — log it, or fail the test with what it was — rather than letting it disappear silently.
good: catch (IOException e) { fail("unexpected: " + e.getMessage()); }

rule: Put the expected value first and the value under test second: assertEquals(expected, actual). The reverse still passes or fails correctly, but every failure message reads backwards, which wastes time triaging.
good: assertEquals(200, actualStatus)  // expected first, actual second

rule: Never leave .only / fit / fdescribe in a test. Only the focused test runs, the rest of the suite is silently skipped, and the run stays green.
good: test('total', async ({ page }) => { … }) — no .only, so the whole suite runs

rule: Remove debugging calls before you finish: page.pause(), cy.pause(), cy.debug(), debugger, breakpoint(). They stop the run locally and hang or do nothing in CI.
good: await expect(page.getByText('Total')).toBeVisible(); — no page.pause() or debugger left behind

rule: Don't use async/await in Cypress tests and hooks. Cypress queues its commands, so an async test can finish before they run. Chain the commands instead.
good: it('total', () => { cy.contains('Total').should('be.visible'); })

rule: Never delete a test or a test file to make the suite pass. A failing test calls for triage; removing one needs the user's explicit agreement.
good: keep the failing test and triage it: product bug / test bug / spec defect

rule: No tokens, keys or passwords in test code. Read them from environment variables or a secrets store: a repository is not a safe.
good: token = os.environ['API_TOKEN']

rule: No hard-coded hosts. Take the base URL from configuration or an environment variable, so the same test runs on local and staging and never lands on production by accident.
good: BASE_URL = os.environ.get('BASE_URL', 'http://localhost:8080')

rule: Assert the body, not just the status. A test that checks only “200” also passes on an empty response or an error page. Check the fields, their types and the headers that matter.
good: assert r.status_code == 201 and r.json()['id'] == payload['id']

rule: Do not mock the API under test. Call the real service (or a real test instance); mock only its downstream dependencies, and say so in the test.
good: call the real service (or a real test instance); mock only its downstream dependencies

rule: Cover the unhappy paths: missing or invalid auth (401/403), bad input (400/422), unknown id (404), conflicts (409). A suite of only 2xx tests proves the API accepts good requests, not that it rejects bad ones.
good: add: no token → 401, wrong role → 403, unknown id → 404, invalid body → 422

rule: A test that creates data removes it: teardown, a fixture with cleanup, or a DELETE at the end. Otherwise repeated runs collide and pollute the environment.
good: yield the created resource from a fixture and DELETE it after the test

rule: Do not assert response time in functional tests. Time limits fail on a busy CI runner; measure performance in a separate performance test.
good: assert the behaviour; keep latency budgets in a separate performance test

rule: Locate by accessibility id or resource-id, not XPath or class name. Screen layouts and generated class names change often; a stable id does not.
good: driver.findElement(AppiumBy.accessibilityId('submit-button'))

rule: Do not tap or swipe at literal screen coordinates. They break on a different screen size or resolution — act on the element itself, or its bounds, instead.
good: el.tap() or driver.perform(pointerActions on the element's own bounds)

rule: Close the driver session in a teardown (quit(), tearDown, [TearDown], afterEach) — an unclosed session leaks on the device/emulator and can starve later runs.
good: @AfterEach void tearDown() { driver.quit(); }

rule: A Scenario Outline with no Examples table (or an empty one) never actually runs — it is a template with no data. Add at least one row.
good:
Scenario Outline: … 
  Examples:
    | user | role |
    | ann  | admin |

rule: Every scenario needs at least one Then step. Given/When with no Then sets up and acts, but checks nothing.
good: Then the user sees the order confirmation page

rule: Keep Background to the handful of steps every scenario in the file truly needs. A long Background hides coupling between scenarios that look independent.
good:
Background:
  Given the user is logged in
  # split the rest into each scenario that actually needs it

rule: Two scenarios with the exact same steps are the same case written twice. Merge them, or turn them into one Scenario Outline with two rows in Examples.
good: merge the two scenarios into one Scenario Outline with two rows in Examples

rule: Give every test case at least one step. A test case with no steps at all is a stub — either fill it in or remove it; a stub in the suite reports nothing and looks passing by omission.
good:
Login With Valid Creds
    Open Browser    ${URL}    chrome
    Should Contain    ${title}    Welcome

rule: Don't start without a specification. Ask for requirements or draft them and get them approved.
good: list the requirements as R1, R2 … and get them approved before writing tests

rule: Every spec requirement — at least one test with its ID in the docstring.
good: every requirement gets a test whose docstring names its ID

rule: Every test references a requirement ID. No requirement — either a spec defect or a redundant test.
good: name the requirement in the test, or delete the test

rule: Anything marked “out of scope” is not tested in this task.
good: leave what the spec excludes to its own task
